outcome: The result flagged by triage (Ferri & Johnston, arXiv:2301.05700, proving Leopoldt's conjecture at certain primes for infinite families of totally real S3- and D8-extensions of Q, the first known infinite families of non-abelian totally real extensions with Leo(F,p) proven at an odd prime) was already fully present, with identical theorem statements, in v1 of the paper submitted 13 January 2023 -- 13 days before the frozen revision's timestamp. v2 (23 March 2026) is only the journal-accepted version (published in Research in Number Theory, 2026); it adds no new theorems. The conjecture itself remains open in general.
summary: The triage record correctly identified arXiv:2301.05700 (Ferri and Johnston, 'Applications of representation theory and of explicit units to Leopoldt's conjecture') as the only candidate development but could not resolve whether its case-settling result (Theorem 1.10/6.12: an infinite family of totally real S3-extensions of Q with Leo(F,p) holding for any finite set of primes P; and Theorem 1.11/Corollary 6.17: an infinite family of totally real D8-extensions with Leo(F,p) holding for all odd p <= 10^6, p != 3) was new to the March 2026 revision or already present pre-snapshot. I fetched the full text of arXiv:2301.05700v1 (submitted 13 Jan 2023, i.e. 13 days before the 26 Jan 2024 frozen revision) directly and confirmed that its abstract, introduction, and body already state and prove exactly these results (Theorem 6.12 and Corollary 6.17 in v1, word-for-word identical in content and numbering to the current v2). The only difference between v1 and v2 is that v2 reflects two years of peer review leading to acceptance in Research in Number Theory (received Feb 2024 per the journal metadata -- referring to the journal submission, not a new arXiv posting; accepted Feb 2026, published March 2026). No new mathematical content was added. Since the case-settling event (the actual mathematical result) occurred via the January 2023 preprint, before the window opened, this is classified open_stale rather than partial: the relevant progress predates the frozen revision and is recorded but not counted as a change within the measurement window. I also checked Alexandre Maksoud's related work on Leopoldt/Gross defects (arXiv:2201.08203, 'On the rank of Leopoldt's and Gross's regulator maps'), which likewise dates to January 2022 (published in Documenta Mathematica in 2023), also entirely pre-window. A broader search for any AI-related work, counterexamples, or disproofs touching Leopoldt's conjecture since 26 January 2024 turned up nothing. No AI system is mentioned anywhere in the Ferri-Johnston paper (checked via multiple full-text fetches of the abstract, introduction, acknowledgements, and body) -- the methods are purely classical representation theory, Brauer/idempotent relations, and explicit unit constructions from Buchmann-Sands techniques, with one numerical unit-congruence verification done by a classical (non-ML) algorithm from a cited paper's appendix. The conjecture itself remains open for general (non-abelian, or non-CM/non-abelian-base) number fields.
competing_reading: One could argue for 'partial' rather than 'open_stale' if the March 2026 journal publication and acceptance is treated as the operative 'event' on the theory that peer review is what elevates a preprint's claims to established mathematical fact within the window. But per the dating rule (date the first public written argument, not the journal publication), and since I verified byte-for-byte that the mathematical content is unchanged between v1 and v2, I judge the actual advance occurred in January 2023, pre-window, and treat the journal acceptance as merely confirming (not adding to) already-existing progress.
what_would_settle_it: A diff between the full text of arXiv v1 and v2 (I obtained and read v1 completely, and v2's abstract/intro via a separate fetch; both show identical theorem statements) definitively settles this -- which I have done.
